items.abstract: <jats:p><strong> Introduction </strong> Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT have transformed how we use artificial intelligence, excelling at tasks like writing essays, answering questions, and even holding conversations. But when it comes to complex reasoning—think solving math problems, tackling commonsense puzzles, or working with symbols—these models often hit a wall.</jats:p>
title: Active Prompting with Chain-of-Thought: Revolutionising Reasoning in Large Language Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dalal and Misra (2024) model a large language model as a compact representation of an enormous multinomial transition matrix and show that next-token generation behaves like Bayesian updating: the pre-trained model supplies a Dirichlet prior, the prompt supplies a likelihood, and the emitted distribution is the posterior. Their analysis is single-step and the prompt is exogenous. This paper extends the framework to multi-step generation, in which the model conditions on text it has itself produced, and in doing so separates two things that the phrase "chain of thought" runs together. A chain of thought is ancestral sampling from the model's own predictive law; in Bayesian terms it performs marginalisation over a latent trace and is a Monte Carlo device. A chain of reasoning conditions on a relation certified outside the model-an arithmetic identity, a retrieved fact, a verifier score-and performs conditioning, supplying a likelihood the model could not have written down. Under self-conditioning the Beta-Bernoulli update becomes a Pólya urn, so the posterior mean of any reasoning mode is a bounded martingale: thinking cannot move the expected probability of being correct, only its dispersion. The nominal posterior nevertheless contracts at rate t-1 while the trace carries exactly zero information about the truth, giving an overconfidence factor 1 + 2t/(α + β), and a Fano bound caps the accuracy of any chain by its exogenous information content. What decomposition does buy is coverage, the relocation of each prediction to a densely visited row of the transition matrix, which holds only within a band [T * , T * * ] of compositional depths. Along the way the Schur-concavity result of Dalal and Misra (2024) generalises to a martingale dilation whose entropy drop equals I(A; Z 1:T | Q); Beta heterogeneity produces a power-law test-time scaling law; self-consistency obeys a Sanov exponent with a bias floor; verified reasoning is sequential importance sampling, with weight degeneracy as its characteristic failure; and optimal chain length obeys a square-root law in the cost of thinking. Three further results sharpen the picture. A Murphy decomposition shows that a thought chain and a reasoning chain generate the same belief movement Var(θ t), but that in the first it is entirely reliability error and in the second entirely resolution. Under an intrinsic time change the chain converges to a Wright-Fisher diffusion run for the finite time 1/(α + β), so belief movement saturates after O(α + β) steps however long the chain is made. And when attention discounts earlier steps at rate γ, the martingale becomes an ergodic process that reverts to the pre-training mean at rate (1γ) 2 (α + β)/{(1γ)(α + β) + 1}, which replaces lock-in by a second pathology, perpetual regression to prior defaults. All parameters of the framework are identified from logged next-token probabilities, and we give closed-form moment estimators.</jats:p>
title: Chain of Reasoning and Thought: Sequential Beta-Dirichlet Updating in Large Language Models
